pages.title: Lock types and lock state machines (SimpleLock, ScatterLock, FileLock, LocalLock)

features.name: Per-object lock catalogue (13 lock types)
features.description: Each CInode carries quiescelock, versionlock (LocalLockC), authlock, linklock, xattrlock, snaplock, flocklock, policylock (SimpleLock), dirfragtreelock, nestlock (ScatterLock/scatterlock), filelock (ScatterLock/filelock); each CDentry carries lock (SimpleLock) and versionlock (LocalLockC). Each lock protects a fixed slice of metadata, carried to replicas via encode_lock_* payloads. CEPH_LOCK_* numeric value = per-object acquisition order.
features.notes: Lock granularity (e.g. filelock lumps size/mtime/atime/layout/client_ranges/inline data/dirstat and all F caps) is a major source of false conflicts.

features.name: SimpleLock state machine (sm_simplelock)
features.description: Stable SYNC (shared read, leases, s caps), LOCK (auth-only, replicas REQ rdlock), EXCL (loner gets sx); transitional SYNC_LOCK, LOCK_SYNC, EXCL_SYNC, EXCL_LOCK, SYNC_EXCL, LOCK_EXCL, SNAP_SYNC; xlock path LOCK_XLOCK -> PREXLOCK -> XLOCK -> XLOCKDONE -> SYNC. Used by DN, IAUTH, ILINK, IXATTR, ISNAP, IFLOCK, IPOLICY; only class with can_remote_xlock.
features.notes: Replicas only see SYNC, SYNC_LOCK, LOCK. LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK row is never used.

features.name: ScatterLock state machine (sm_scatterlock) for nestlock and dirfragtreelock
features.description: Stable SYNC (read everywhere), LOCK (auth-only write), MIX (write on every rank, no reads); transitions SYNC_LOCK, LOCK_SYNC, SYNC_MIX/SYNC_MIX2, MIX_SYNC, MIX_LOCK/MIX_LOCK2 (two-stage), TSYN family unimplemented. scatter_eval keeps INEST in MIX when replicated, LOCK otherwise; IDFT goes SYNC unless the inode has delegated dirfrags.
features.notes: Table lacks a MIX_SYNC2 row although replicas enter that state; no caps ever issued for these locks.

features.name: FileLock state machine (sm_filelock)
features.description: filelock adds EXCL (loner Fsxcrwb), XSYN family (loner keeps Fcb while auth rdlocks), xlock states (XLOCK returns to LOCK), XLOCKSNAP, PRE_SCAN/SCAN (size recovery), MIX (Frwl uncached shared I/O), SYNC (Fscrl). file_eval chooses EXCL for one writer, MIX for multiple writers or writer+readers, SYNC for readers.
features.notes: Fa (WREXTEND) is never issued by any state; Fl only in SYNC/MIX family.

features.name: LocalLock (versionlock, quiescelock)
features.description: Always-LOCK local locks: wrlock shared, xlock exclusive with wrlocks, queued xlocker blocks new wrlockers. versionlock auto-wrlocked by leaders next to xlocks (pipelining), xlocked by peers (safe rollback, also for remote-xlock peer requests); quiescelock auto-wrlocked once per acquire_locks on the inode of the first xlock/wrlock/remote-wrlock op whose lock has a cap shift (unless skip_quiesce), xlocked by quiesce_inode; local_xlock_finish on IQUIESCE re-evaluates cap locks; rdlock on a local lock asserts.
features.notes: last_wrlock_client of versionlock decides projected-value visibility in encode_inodestat.

features.name: Lock state to allowed client caps
features.description: gcaps_allowed(CAP_ANY|CAP_LONER|CAP_XLOCKER) per state (caps/loner_caps/xlocker_caps/replica_caps columns), composed per inode over authlock(<<2), linklock(<<4), xattrlock(<<6), filelock(<<8), masked by quarantine and quiesce; xlocker extras limited to s|x|c|r (file) or s|x. Transitions revoke to the transitional state's caps; gather completes when issued caps fit the next state's caps. Locker::get_allowed_caps (issue_caps) grants xlocker extras to any client that is the xlocker, while CInode::get_caps_allowed_for_client (reply-time caps in encode_inodestat) grants them only to the loner.
features.notes: is_loner_mode() uses the current state even when evaluating the next state's caps.

features.name: Loner selection and exclusive caps
features.description: calc_ideal_loner picks the unique non-stale client cap (dirs: any cap without delegated dirfrags; files: wanting WR or Fr); none if read-only or a replica rank wants caps. Loner id copied into excl_client of the four cap locks; try_drop_loner only when the loner's issued caps fit non-loner allowance.
features.notes: Directory loner (EXCL) enables Fx on directories, prerequisite for async dirops.

features.name: Gather engine (eval_gather)
features.description: Completes transitions when gather_set empty, local rd/wr/x/lease holders compatible with next state, no writebehind in flight, issued caps fit next state, file recovery done; replica sends LOCKACK/MIXACK/SYNCACK; auth runs two-stage MIX_LOCK, writebehind, start_scatter/AC_MIX or AC_SYNC; then set next, auth_unpin, drop loner, wake waiters, try_eval, issue caps.
features.notes: Triggered by lock releases, cap acks, lease release/expiry, replica acks, stale-session revocation, recovery completion.

features.name: Stable-state policy evaluation
features.description: try_eval/eval route stable auth locks to simple_eval (loner wants x -> EXCL, else SYNC unless WAIT_WR waiters), scatter_eval (INEST MIX/LOCK, IDFT SYNC), file_eval (EXCL/MIX/SYNC by wanted caps); deferred while frozen/freezing except DN/ISNAP/IPOLICY and scatter_wanted; read-only FS forces SYNC.
features.notes: Heuristics; client-visible through cap grants.

features.name: xlock lifecycle with XLOCKDONE early-reply visibility
features.description: xlock_start drives LOCK -> LOCK_XLOCK -> PREXLOCK -> XLOCK; early reply sets XLOCKDONE (xlocker may read, rdlock, lease, hold s caps, re-xlock except IFILE); after commit xlock_finish -> _finish_xlock -> EXCL for target loner or eval_gather to next (simple: SYNC with AC_SYNC data; file: LOCK); cancel_locking handles aborts.
features.notes: Other clients wait until the change is journaled. No early reply (so no XLOCKDONE) when mds_early_reply=false, mdr->no_early_reply, journaled peers, alloc_ino, MDS-originated requests or replays (Server::early_reply).

features.name: Remote xlock and remote wrlock via peer requests
features.description: Replica leader sends MMDSPeerRequest OP_XLOCK (simplelock only) or OP_WRLOCK (src dir filelock/nestlock in cross-rank rename); auth acquires via acquire_locks(skip_quiesce) as a peer (so the object's versionlock is xlocked) and acks (XLOCKACK carries lock data); OP_UNXLOCK/OP_UNWRLOCK/OP_DROPLOCKS release. Replica stays in LOCK; auth stays in XLOCK (peer requests never early-reply).
features.notes: MDS-to-MDS only.

features.name: Inter-MDS MLock protocol
features.description: MSG_MDS_LOCK (0x300) with actions SYNC(-1), MIX(-2), LOCK(-3), LOCKFLUSHED(-4) auth->replica and SYNCACK(1), MIXACK(2), LOCKACK(3), REQSCATTER(7), REQUNSCATTER(8, never sent), NUDGE(9), REQRDLOCK(10) replica->auth; payload asker, action, reqid (unused), lock_type, MDSCacheObjectInfo, lockdata.
features.notes: Not an external contract; Rust MDS may replace it.

features.name: Replica-initiated lock requests (REQRDLOCK, REQSCATTER, NUDGE)
features.description: Replicas cannot change state; they ask the auth: REQRDLOCK -> simple_sync (or retry when stable), REQSCATTER -> scatter_mix or scatter_wanted, NUDGE -> scatter_nudge on the auth. Requesters hold remote auth pins to prevent freezing.

features.name: Scatter-gather of directory dirstat (filelock on directories)
features.description: Dirfrag fragstat vs accounted_fragstat deltas folded into inode dirstat (nfiles, nsubdirs, mtime, change_attr) on gather with version epochs; validated against fragment sums; dirty data written behind with EUpdate scatter_writebehind.
features.notes: Directory mtime/ctime updates are POSIX-visible; counts used for rmdir emptiness; propagated synchronously on one rank, scattered across ranks.

features.name: Scatter-gather of recursive stats (nestlock)
features.description: rstat deltas (rbytes, rfiles, rsubdirs, rsnaps, rctime) pushed from children into dirfrags and from dirfrags into inodes; deferred via dirty_rstat_inodes, mark_updated_scatterlock and LogSegment dirty_dirfrag_nest; gathered by scatter_nudge; quota broadcast after updates.
features.notes: Feeds ceph.dir.r* vxattrs and quota realms; freshness lags across ranks.

features.name: Dirfragtree scatter (dirfragtreelock)
features.description: Ranks that fragment a dirfrag they own but whose inode they do not own mark STATE_DIRTYDFT and the inode dftlock dirty; on gather the auth forces reported frags to leaves and journals the new tree.

features.name: Scatter writebehind and flush flags
features.description: scatter_writebehind takes a forced wrlock, projects the inode, sums deltas, sets FLUSHING, journals EUpdate(scatter_writebehind); finish applies, sets FLUSHED, unpins PIN_DIRTYSCATTERED, removes inode from LogSegment dirty lists, sends LOCKFLUSHED to replicas in MIX_LOCK*/MIX_EXCL, drops the wrlock to continue the gather.

features.name: Scatter nudging (scatter_tick, scatter_nudge, log segment expiry)
features.description: Dirty scatterlocks queued in updated_scatterlocks are nudged by scatter_tick after mds_scatter_nudge_interval (5 s) every mds_tick_interval (5 s); LogSegment::try_to_expire nudges inodes on dirty_dirfrag_* lists so segments can trim; replicas send LOCK_AC_NUDGE.
features.notes: Determines rstat/dirstat freshness across ranks and journal trimming.

features.name: Dentry leases bound to DN lock state
features.description: Leases only on dentries: issued when dn lock can_lease and dir filelock cannot (not SYNC) and client lacks dir Fs/Fx; LEASED flag on dn lock; revoked (MClientLease REVOKE mask 1) when the DN lock leaves lease states; gather waits for REVOKE_ACK/RELEASE or 30 s expiry.
features.notes: Lease duration pool 1 = 30 s, not configurable.

features.name: SNAP_SYNC gating of snapshotted inodes
features.description: cow_inode puts the four cap locks of a snapped inode into SNAP_SYNC with forced wrlocks until all clients with dirty data flush snaps; readers of the snapshot wait and kick the head inode's lock.
features.notes: Snapshots are a Ceph extension.

features.name: XLOCKSNAP for truncate with pending snapflush
features.description: truncate_inode moves an xlocked filelock to XLOCKSNAP to revoke Fb before truncating while snapflushes are pending; eval_gather waits for Fb to be gone.

features.name: PRE_SCAN/SCAN file size recovery
features.description: After failover, files with client_ranges whose clients did not reconnect enter PRE_SCAN -> SCAN, file caps are revoked, RecoveryQueue probes object sizes, then the lock moves to LOCK; the filelock admits no rdlock/wrlock/xlock meanwhile (requests that need it prioritize the inode in the recovery queue).
features.notes: Gives correct size/mtime after writer crash.

features.name: XSYN (rdlock against a buffering loner)
features.description: _rdlock_kick moves a file filelock in EXCL with a target loner to XSYN instead of SYNC (unless anonymous): loner keeps Fcb, loses Fs/Fx/Fr/Fw, auth may rdlock.

features.name: Lock waiters (FIFO, per-lock wait bits)
features.description: Waiters stored on the parent object in a 128-bit mask (lock bits at 64 + 4*k); WAIT_RD, WAIT_WR, WAIT_XLOCK=WAIT_STABLE, WAIT_REMOTEXLOCK; ordered by a global sequence; completed synchronously by finish_waiters or deferred via pfinishers.
features.notes: Head-of-line blocking: one pending xlock blocks later readers.

features.name: Lock state across replication, export and rejoin
features.description: replica_state encoding for new replicas; export encodes full state + gather set + loner and twiddles exporter to replica state; rejoin encodes scatter states specially and marks NEED_RECOVER; auth infers MIX/LOCK from strong rejoins; acquire_locks waits for cluster recovery before rdlocking NEED_RECOVER locks.
features.notes: Lock states are never persisted.

features.name: Reconnect-time lock state choice
features.description: choose_lock_states picks EXCL/MIX/LOCK/SYNC from reconnected clients' issued (and dirty) caps and scatter dirtiness, and chooses a loner if write/excl caps exist.
features.notes: Clients keep their caps across MDS failover.

features.name: Lock caches interplay
features.description: Locks referenced by MDLockCache objects carry the CACHED flag; transitions that must gather rd/wr locks invalidate lock caches (revoking the related dir caps) first.
features.notes: Async dirops support.

features.name: Replica-wanted caps (MInodeFileCaps)
features.description: Replica ranks forward their clients' wanted caps (filtered by allowed_ever) to the auth; auth stores mds_caps_wanted, which disables the loner and contributes to other_wanted in file_eval.

features.name: Forced wrlocks for cap flushes and max_size
features.description: Cap flush updates take wrlock_force on filelock/authlock/xattrlock for the journal duration (state is ignored). can_force_wrlock is consulted only in _do_cap_update for a client's max_size change on a head inode: it lets the change proceed in EXCL_SYNC/EXCL_LOCK (XCL = loner or xlocker); the SNAP_SYNC column is never consulted (snapshotted inodes only). Otherwise file_excl/simple_lock is started and the update waits (C_MDL_CheckMaxSize on WAIT_STABLE).
features.notes: Avoids deadlock between a transition waiting for a cap ack and the ack needing a lock.

features.name: Journal flush to release locks (nudge_log)
features.description: When requests wait on unstable locks held by uncommitted requests, the Locker flushes the MDLog (nudge_log, simple_sync with wrlocks, MLock handlers, scatter_tick, writebehind).

features.name: Projected-value visibility in replies
features.description: encode_inodestat returns projected (uncommitted) inode fields only to the client that xlocks the relevant lock, the loner, or (versionlock) the last wrlocking client; dentry projected linkage only to the xlocking client/request.
features.notes: Read-your-writes before durability; other clients see committed values.

features.name: Admin introspection of locks
features.description: dump inode / dump cache print each lock's state, gather set, rd/wr/x counts, xlock_by; dump_ops_in_flight shows acquire_locks wait events; lock path command acquires arbitrary locks for tests/quiesce.

features.name: Quiesce interaction
features.description: Ops that wrlock/xlock cap-bearing locks implicitly wrlock quiescelock; quiesce xlocks it; quiesced inodes restrict caps to ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p; peer lock requests skip the quiesce lock.
features.notes: Used for subvolume quiesce (snapshot consistency groups).

features.name: Read-only filesystem lock policy
features.description: When the MDCache is read-only all policy functions force SYNC and no loner is chosen.

features.name: Dead or unimplemented lock machinery
features.description: TSYN family (scatter_tempsync aborts), LOCK_REMOTEXLOCK, sm_t.careful/gcaps_careful/get_caps_careful, SimpleLock::req_rdlock_from_auth (REQ is only documentation), can_scatter_pin, do_import, eval_scatter_gathers, LOCK_AC_REQUNSCATTER sender, LOCK_AC_FOR_* macros, MLock::reqid.
features.notes: Can be dropped in a reimplementation.

features.name: Early-reply lock release and journal flush policy
features.description: After submitting the journal entry of an early-replied request, Server::journal_and_reply calls Locker::handle_locks_for_early_reply: all rdlocks are released except snaplock/policylock rdlocks (kept so a later mksnap/setlayout on another rank waits for the unsafe request), and the journal is nudged if a held lock is unstable with waiters. Requests without an early reply flush the journal immediately. Wrlocks and xlocks are held until the request is safe.
features.notes: Determines how long other clients wait behind an unsafe request (journal latency) and the read-your-writes window.

features.name: Request-embedded cap and dentry-lease releases
features.description: Client requests carry ceph_mds_request_release records (e.g. kclient drops Fs|Ax|Xx on the parent dir unless it holds Fx, plus its dentry lease); Server::handle_client_request applies them via Locker::process_request_cap_release before any lock is taken, so the requester's own caps/leases never have to be revoked by the transition its request triggers.
features.notes: Skipped for replayed requests; the cap part is deferred until unfreeze if the inode is freezing/frozen (should_defer_client_cap_frozen).

features.name: Replica dentry readability and linkage propagation
features.description: Replica DN locks mirror the auth (SYNC readable, LOCK not readable); path traversal on a replica waits WAIT_RD (perf counter traverse_lock) while the auth holds the dentry in LOCK/XLOCK*. The DN lock payload carries linkage but replicas only adopt 'first'; linkage changes reach replicas via MDentryLink/MDentryUnlink.
features.notes: MDS-internal; relevant for cross-shard dentry visibility design.

features.name: Stale-session cap revocation vs lock gathers
features.description: When a session goes stale, caps that are being revoked are revoked forcibly so lock gathers can finish; if write caps (CEPH_CAP_ANY_WR) are among them the client is evicted instead (revoke_stale_cap evicts directly; revoke_stale_caps returns false and find_idle_sessions evicts it as laggy unless OSDs are laggy). A forcibly revoked client with a writable client_range marks the inode NEEDSRECOVER, so the next filelock gather waits for size recovery.
features.notes: No lock-level timeout for live clients; only mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout (default 0) evicts non-responders.

serialization_points.name: mds_lock around all lock state
serialization_points.why_serialized: lock objects have no internal synchronization; all Locker code, contexts and journal completions run under the rank-wide mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: True scope is one lock instance plus its parent object, waiters and the caps/leases of that object's clients.

serialization_points.name: Per-lock state machine transitions
serialization_points.why_serialized: a lock is in exactly one state; incompatible requests wait until the transition completes
serialization_points.notes: rd/wr/x conflicts are real but locks lump unrelated fields (filelock = size, mtime, atime, layout, client_ranges, inline data, dirstat, all F caps).

serialization_points.name: FIFO lock waiters (head-of-line blocking)
serialization_points.why_serialized: unstable states deny new compatible requests too (e.g. readers behind a pending xlock waiting for a slow client)
serialization_points.notes: Fairness prevents writer starvation, but stalls readers behind slow cap revocations.

serialization_points.name: Replica gather
serialization_points.why_serialized: auth waits for every replica's ack before changing state
serialization_points.notes: Ranks below REJOIN stay in the gather set until they rejoin.

serialization_points.name: Client cap revocation gather
serialization_points.shared_state: issued caps of all clients on the inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: transition completes only when every client acked revocation of caps the next state forbids
serialization_points.notes: Required for POSIX coherence; no lock-level timeout; kclient defers ack until writeback.

serialization_points.name: Dentry lease revocation gather
serialization_points.why_serialized: DN lock cannot leave lease-allowing states until leases are released or expire
serialization_points.notes: Up to 30 s for an unresponsive client; expiry is only checked when the upkeep thread trims the cache (MDCache::trim_client_leases, every ~mds_cache_trim_interval).

serialization_points.name: Directory filelock/nestlock wrlock by namespace changes
serialization_points.shared_state: parent directory inode filelock/nestlock, dirfrag fnode
serialization_points.why_serialized: every create/unlink/rename in a directory wrlocks the dir filelock and nestlock; entering LOCK/MIX revokes Fs from all clients and any gather stops all namespace changes until wrlocks drain and writebehind commits
serialization_points.notes: wrlocks are shared so creates run concurrently; the cost is the transitions.

serialization_points.name: Scatter-gather of dirstat/rstat
serialization_points.shared_state: inode dirstat/rstat, fragment accounted stats, version epoch
serialization_points.why_serialized: gather needs all wrlocks drained and a journaled writebehind before readers see the sum
serialization_points.notes: Values are commutative deltas; could be aggregated asynchronously.

serialization_points.name: rstat propagation up the tree
serialization_points.why_serialized: each level needs a nestlock wrlock and versionlock to project the parent inode; throttled by mds_dirstat_min_interval
serialization_points.notes: Falls back to scatter (deferred) when busy or cross-rank.

serialization_points.name: Path-wide snaplock/policylock rdlocks
serialization_points.why_serialized: snapshot and layout/quota changes xlock these; every request below must hold rdlocks along the path
serialization_points.notes: mksnap needs a consistent cut; other ops only need a stable snaprealm/layout epoch.

serialization_points.name: versionlock pipelining and peer exclusion
serialization_points.why_serialized: leader wrlocks to pipeline, peers xlock to keep rollback safe

serialization_points.name: quiescelock
serialization_points.why_serialized: ops touching cap-bearing locks take it shared; quiesce takes it exclusive

serialization_points.name: Global updated_scatterlocks list and scatter_tick
serialization_points.why_serialized: single list walked by the tick

serialization_points.name: Cross-client visibility waits for journal commit
serialization_points.why_serialized: other clients may not see unjournaled changes; lock released only at request finish

serialization_points.name: Freeze vs unstable locks
serialization_points.why_serialized: each transitional auth lock holds an auth pin, blocking freezes (export, fragmentation); frozen objects defer transitions

serialization_points.name: Synchronous waiter execution
serialization_points.why_serialized: state changes run retried requests inline (re-entrancy)

serialization_points.name: Replica dentry reads blocked by auth DN lock transitions
serialization_points.shared_state: replica copy of a dentry's DN lock
serialization_points.why_serialized: while the auth xlocks a dentry (create/unlink/rename) its replicas are in LOCK (can_read=AUTH) and every traversal through that name on other ranks waits for LOCK_AC_SYNC
serialization_points.notes: Only operations on the same name truly conflict; the wait also covers the journal commit of the xlocking request.

external_contract.item: Cap bits granted per lock state
external_contract.detail: filelock SYNC: Fscrl any/Fscr replica; LOCK: Fcb; MIX: Frwl (uncached shared I/O); EXCL: loner Fsxcrwb only; XSYN: loner Fcb; simple locks SYNC: s, EXCL: loner sx, XLOCKDONE: xlocker s. Fa never issued; only one client holds x bits.
kclient defers MClientCaps ack of Fb/Fc revocation until writeback/invalidate completes; MDS lock gathers block until the ack arrives (no lock-level timeout).
Fs on a directory lets kclient cache it as complete; the flag is cleared when Fs is issued or revoked; namespace changes by others move dir filelock out of SYNC/EXCL and revoke Fs.

MDS sends MClientLease CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE (mask 1, seq, dir ino, dir first, last=NOSNAP, dname); kclient replies CEPH_MDS_LEASE_REVOKE_ACK reusing the message, even if the dentry is gone; MDS removes the lease if seq matches.
libcephfs answers CEPH_MDS_LEASE_RELEASE; it drops its lease only if mask & CEPH_LEASE_VALID; MDS treats RELEASE like REVOKE_ACK.

kclient sends getattr to the auth MDS when the requested mask has any s bit while it holds any x cap on the inode ((mask & CEPH_CAP_ANY_SHARED) && (issued & CEPH_CAP_ANY_EXCL)), or when asking CEPH_STAT_RSTAT or Xs, to avoid replica-triggered lock transitions.
MetaRequest::auth_is_best mirrors the kclient rule (any s bit requested while holding any x cap, or RSTAT/Xs requested -> auth); OPEN and READDIR and write ops always go to the auth.

After an unsafe reply the requesting client sees projected values and may hold s caps on the xlocked lock (XLOCKDONE); other clients block until the request is journaled and finished and get non-projected values in replies. Exception found: MClientQuota (broadcast_quota_to_client) carries the projected rstat.
Same XLOCKDONE semantics as for kclient; affects NFS-Ganesha consistency across exports.
Several clients writing one file push filelock to MIX: Fr|Fw without Fc/Fb, i.e. synchronous uncached I/O through libcephfs.

ceph.dir.rbytes/rfiles/rsubdirs/rctime come from the auth's inode rstat; across ranks they lag by mds_scatter_nudge_interval (5 s) plus tick; on one rank ancestors above the first level may lag by mds_dirstat_min_interval (1 s).
Dentry leases last 30 s (pool 1 of client_lease_durations); renew answered only while the DN lock still allows leases.
During filelock LOCK/XLOCK clients may keep Fc/Fb; truncation is pushed with CEPH_CAP_OP_TRUNC.

external_contract.item: No error codes for lock contention
external_contract.detail: Requests blocked by lock states wait indefinitely (retried internally); no EAGAIN; only eviction/session policies end the wait.

dump inode/dump cache include per-lock gather_set, state name (get_state_name strings such as sync, lock, mix, excl, sync->lock, xlockdone), type, is_leased, num_rdlocks, num_wrlocks, num_xlocks, xlock_by.
dump_ops_in_flight shows events like 'failed to rdlock, waiting', 'failed to xlock, waiting', 'acquired locks'.
asok 'lock path <path> [type:r|w|x ...]' with ap_dont_block/ap_freeze/await/lifetime options; returns -EAGAIN when ap_dont_block aborts.
While a subvolume is quiesced (quiescelock xlocked by quiesce op), clients only get ANY_RD|Fc|Fb|p; ops needing cap-bearing locks block.
PRE_SCAN/SCAN recovery probes file data objects to recover size/mtime of files whose writers did not reconnect.

kclient attaches releases of parent-directory caps (r_dentry_drop, e.g. Fs|Ax|Xx for mknod/mkdir, Fs|Xx for unlink/rename, unless holding Fx) and its dentry lease to namespace requests; the MDS must apply them before taking locks.

Without a dentry lease, kclient trusts a cached dentry while the directory holds Fs and the dentry's lease_shared_gen equals the dir's i_shared_gen (bumped whenever Fs is newly issued). Revoking Fs from a directory therefore invalidates all such dentries.
In MIX the MDS may issue Fl next to Fr|Fw when wanted; the kclient uses its page cache if it holds Fc or Fl, otherwise reads synchronously from OSDs.

rust_implications.implication: The C++ lock semantics are fully table-driven (locks.c). A Rust MDS can keep const per-class tables but should drop unused states (TSYN family, REMOTEXLOCK), the dead careful field and avoid undefined rows (scatterlock MIX_SYNC2, XLOCK) by construction (exhaustive enums).
A lock's transitions only touch its parent object, its waiters and the caps/leases of that object's clients; lock state can be owned by the shard that owns the inode/dentry, with no global mutex.

Model each transitional state as an awaitable set of conditions (local holders drained, replica acks, per-client cap acks, lease releases, recovery done, journal flush) instead of re-evaluating with eval_gather on every trigger; never run waiter continuations re-entrantly inside the state change.

dirstat/rstat are commutative deltas with a version epoch; per-shard delta counters aggregated asynchronously avoid lock transitions that stall every create/unlink in a directory. Only exact consumers (rmdir emptiness, readdir completeness, snapshot COW, quota) need a barrier/epoch read.

Clients only see caps: keep the exact per-state cap sets (one loner with x bits, Fs revoked before others mutate, MIX = Fr|Fw without Fc/Fb, Fl only for lazy opens, never Fa), cap revoke/grant sequencing, and kclient's reliance on directory Fs for dir-complete caching.

XLOCKDONE semantics are externally visible: the requesting client sees its own unsafe changes (projected values, s caps), others must not see them before the journal commit. A Rust design with per-shard journals must provide the same guarantee (e.g. visibility epochs per client).

Dentry leases only; 30 s TTL; issue only when the directory cannot be cached via Fs; revoke mask must intersect CEPH_LEASE_VALID (libcephfs); accept REVOKE_ACK and RELEASE with matching seq; expiry must unblock transitions.

C++ FIFO waiters let one xlock waiting on an unresponsive client stall all later readers of the lock; the Rust lock manager should keep fairness but bound the damage (timeouts per subvolume SLA, revocation deadlines, or letting compatible readers of unaffected fields proceed with finer-grained locks).

rust_implications.topic: Directory locks as the scaling bottleneck
rust_implications.implication: Every namespace change wrlocks the parent dir filelock+nestlock; transitions from SYNC revoke Fs from all clients and gathers block all creates. For Ganesha/NFS create-heavy workloads, keep directory mutation concurrency shared (IX-style intents) and decouple dirstat aggregation from the dir cap state.

snaplock/policylock are rdlocked on every ancestor for every request; replace with an RCU/epoch snapshot of snaprealm/layout per subvolume shard, with a quiesce-style barrier only for mksnap/layout changes.
Locks of early-replied requests are held until journal commit; Rust per-shard journals must flush promptly when someone waits on such locks (equivalent of nudge_log) to keep cross-client latency low.

C++ never persists lock state; after restart it derives states from reconnected caps (choose_lock_state) and runs size recovery (PRE_SCAN/SCAN) for files with client_ranges whose clients did not reconnect. A Rust MDS needs equivalent reconnect-driven lock initialization and file size probing.

MLock, MInodeFileCaps and peer lock ops are MDS-internal; with no C++ coexistence the Rust MDS can use a different cross-shard protocol (e.g. 2PC with shard-owned authority) as long as client-visible caps/leases/replies stay compatible.

MIX-like shared-write state with per-shard accumulation is what lets multiple writers proceed; keep such a state for files with multiple writers (Ganesha), granting Fr|Fw without caching, without needing a global lock.

kclient/libcephfs send getattr to the auth MDS (as known from their caps/subtree map) when holding x caps or requesting RSTAT/Xs; any shard placement must keep a single, discoverable authority per inode.

No lock-level timeout exists in C++ (only optional mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout, default 0). Per-subvolume QoS/SLA needs explicit revocation deadlines and eviction policy so one tenant's client cannot stall another tenant's locks.
C++ rstat lags 5-10 s across ranks; tools and users tolerate this. A Rust MDS may be fresher but should keep rctime/rbytes semantics and quota broadcast behaviour.
C++ implements quiesce as an implicit shared wrlock on every cap-related op plus an xlock by quiesce and a cap mask; in a sharded design a per-subvolume barrier/epoch is the natural equivalent.
C++ waiters are FIFO via a global sequence; replicate fairness per lock but avoid a global counter.

Apply ceph_mds_request_release records (cap drops and dentry-lease drops) before planning/acquiring locks for a request, otherwise the request's own client must be sent a revoke and the operation waits a client round trip.

C++ releases rdlocks at early reply but keeps snaplock/policylock rdlocks and all wrlocks/xlocks until journal commit, and flushes the journal lazily unless someone waits. A Rust transaction engine with early replies needs the same split (what is visible early vs. after commit) and a 'waiter present -> flush now' trigger per shard journal.

rust_implications.topic: Separate linkage propagation from lock state
rust_implications.implication: C++ replicas never apply linkage from the DN lock payload; linkage travels in MDentryLink/MDentryUnlink while the DN lock only gates readability. With shard-owned dentries this can collapse into one ordered per-shard update stream.

open_questions: Confirm by test that the 'lock path' admin command with nest:x or dft:x aborts the MDS: by code reading simple_xlock moves the scatterlock into LOCK_XLOCK/PREXLOCK, which are all-zero ('stable') rows in scatterlock[], and the next xlock_start iteration calls simple_lock whose switch hits ceph_abort().

Is the missing MIX_SYNC2 row in scatterlock[] intentional? Replicas of nestlock/dirfragtreelock sit in an all-zero 'stable' state until AC_SYNC; no path calling eval_gather on it was found, but this was not exhaustively proven.
Rationale for simplelock LOCK_EXCL allowing 's' caps to any client (caps column) is undocumented.
Both kclient and libcephfs comments claim replicas return stale xattrs after setxattr; MDS code sends xattrs to replicas on XLOCK->SYNC via AC_SYNC data. Is the claim still accurate?
scatter_mix from LOCK switches to MIX without gathering Fc/Fb revocation: is there a coherence window where a client keeps buffered data while other ranks write (unverified impact)?
When eval_gather defers waiters into pfinishers, try_eval runs before the woken requests; could a lock bounce (e.g. LOCK -> SYNC before a waiting xlocker retries)? Not verified.

Does the two-stage MIX->LOCK gather still provide the cross-MDS rename safety described in commit c3a40829d71, given that auth wrlocks no longer block the local stage? Current rename code instead takes remote wrlocks on the source dir's filelock/nestlock at the source dirfrag auth (Server::rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn), which blocks the replica's MIX_LOCK ack; whether this covers the 'third MDS is srcdiri auth' case from the commit message is unverified.

By code reading, a replica nestlock/dirfragtreelock in the row-less MIX_SYNC2 state looks stable, so a local wrlock attempt sends LOCK_AC_REQSCATTER; if it reaches the auth while still in MIX_SYNC it sets scatter_wanted and the auth goes back toward MIX right after reaching SYNC. Not tested whether this causes noticeable lock ping-pong under mixed readdir/create load across ranks.

set_xlocks_done asserts every xlocked object is auth; this relies on remote-xlocking operations (cross-rank link/unlink/rename) always having journaled peers (which suppresses early reply). No explicit check enforces it; not proven for every path.
